summary: Richard Hughes Seager works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD), and was appointed Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College around 1994.

Richard J. Davidson studied at Midwood High School, New York University (~1968–1972), and Harvard University (~1972–1976). He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987, 1996, and from 2001 to 2017 as a psychology professor.
Richard Jay Kohn was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1988 under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and studied under Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

Richard K. Payne works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata, served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1993–2017), and held posts at the Graduate Theological Union and Numata Center.
Richard Keith Sprigg was a scholar in linguistics and Tibetology. He studied at Oakham School and held a post at the University of London and SOAS University of London from circa 1948 to 1980.

Richard Kieckhefer, a scholar of religious studies and history, earned his undergraduate degree at Saint Louis University and his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin. He joined Northwestern University in 1975 and served as president of Societas Magica and ASCH.

Richard King specializes in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster universities (PhD under Daniel Mariau), and held posts at the University of Stirling (~1993–2002), Vanderbilt University (~2002–2009), and the University of Glasgow (~2009–2011).

Richard M. Jaffe works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held a post at North Carolina State University (~1995–2000) before serving as Professor of Religious Studies at Duke University from circa 2000.

Richard Morris was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied at Battersea Training College. He held posts at King's College School (1869), Dedham Grammar School (~1871–1875), and was headmaster of the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875–1888).

Richard P. Boyle completed graduate work at the University of Washington and studied under Kyozan Joshu Sasaki. He taught at the University of California, Los Angeles, and was affiliated with the University of New Mexico (attested 2015).

Richard P. Hayes is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal, Shoryu Katsura, and T. Venkatacharya, holding posts at Toronto, McGill University, and the University of New Mexico.

Richard Payne works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996, 2007) and held affiliations with the University of Chicago (attested 2021) and Numata Center (attested 2026).
Richard Peter Hottelet was active in Buddhist studies, studying under Narayan Hemandas Samtani and holding an attested post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1971.
Richard Phené Spiers was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at King's College London from circa 1856 to 1858 and at Beaux-Arts de Paris from circa 1858 to 1861.

Richard Pischel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Kiel University (1875), Halle-Wittenberg (1885–1902), Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1908), and the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

Richard Polenberg was a historian who studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University (PhD). He served as Professor of American History at Cornell University from 1966 to 2011 and as a Fulbright Visiting Professor at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1974–1975).

Richard Schmidt was an Indologist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel, Karl Friedrich Geldner, and Ernst Mehliß. He held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1898–1908), the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1904–1910), and the University of Münster (1910).
Richard Shilleto, active in linguistics, was educated at Repton School, Shrewsbury School (~1823–1828), and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1828–1832). He also taught Robert Alexander Neil.

Richard Sproat works in computational linguistics and Indology. He studied at UC San Diego (1977–1981) and MIT (1981–1985), and held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (2003–2009), Oregon Health and Science University (2009–2012), and Google (2012).

Richard Sylvan was a philosopher who studied at Victoria University of Wellington (~1954–1958) and Princeton University (~1959–1963). He held posts at the University of Sydney (~1963–1964) and the Australian National University (fellow in 1971).
